- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates downward momentum or fails to account for seasonal/structural trends.
- Forecasts often lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the forecast window (days 10–20), indicating delayed reaction to news or market sentiment.
- Model tends to ignore recent low-price periods (e.g., 70–75 range) and fails to adjust forecasts downward when prices are consolidating or trending lower — underestimates “support” levels.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts with a sharp peak, then fails to correct — overestimates volatility or misjudges “peak” timing.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low prices on future forecasts — fails to recognize that low prices can trigger sustained downward pressure or mean reversion.
